title: When the Orchard Breaks
premise: In the winter of 1794, Theo Delacroix carries sealed dispatches from a collapsing republic across the mountains, posing as an orchard surveyor. Stranded when the seasonal bridge closes, they shelter with the Vasseur family — a widowed innkeeper, her two grown children, and a fugitive printer hiding in the cellar — and slowly stop being a courier and start being kin. When the ice begins to break early, a single berth on the last ferry south forces Theo to choose between delivering the dispatches that could save the republic's remnant, saving the printer who has become a brother, or saving themselves. In the end Theo gives up the codes, burns them unread, and stays behind as the ferry pulls away — choosing the fragile, chosen family over history's grand machinery.
about_author: Ivo Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from refugees of the revolutionary era. They write about ordinary people caught in the gears of history from a farmhouse that once, allegedly, hid a printing press.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Theo crosses the mountains under a false name, carrying dispatches sewn into their coat lining, convinced they are merely a vessel for other people's history. An avalanche detour delivers them to the Vasseur inn at dusk just as officials announce the bridge will close within days. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: wary detachment beginning to crack at the warmth of strangers' lamplight.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Trapped by the closing bridge, Theo discovers the printer, Aurélien, hidden beneath the inn's floorboards and helps conceal him during a garrison search, binding their fates together. Marguerite Vasseur's daughter Camille teaches Theo to graft apple cuttings, an act of faith in a future Theo doesn't believe in. POV: alternating Theo and Camille. Emotional beat: found family taking root before anyone admits it.

chapters.title: Ice Breaking Early
chapters.summary: A warm wind cracks the river ice weeks ahead of schedule; a government agent arrives offering one guaranteed berth on the final ferry — in exchange for the printer. Marguerite refuses to choose among her children, so the impossible decision falls to Theo, whose dispatches could buy three berths but doom Aurélien. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the climax — love against duty made literal, a choice with no clean hands.

chapters.title: Grafts and Ashes
chapters.summary: Theo burns the dispatches unread, trades the agent their own berth for Aurélien's passage, and watches the ferry carry their chosen family south while they remain with Marguerite and Camille among the bare orchards. Spring comes; the first grafted bud opens. POV: Theo, closing with Camille's letter arriving months later. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity finally self-made, belonging chosen over survival.
